title: Telekom Malaysia gets regulatory nod for RM2.7 bil submarine cable project
text:
Telekom Malaysia gets regulatory nod for RM2.7 bil submarine cable project Tuesday 17 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Tech Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 17): Telekom Malaysia Bhd (KL: TM ) has received the nod to build a submarine cable project linking Peninsular Malaysia, Sarawak and Sabah, with approved cost of up to RM2.7 billion.
 According to the notification issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), TM Technology Services Sdn Bhd, a wholly owned subsidiary, was designated as the universal service provider for Part 1 of the project dubbed SALAM.
 The project is scheduled to begin on Dec 15 with phased completion targeted by the first quarter of 2030, Telekom Malaysia said in a bourse filing on Tuesday.
 The SALAM initiative was first opened for proposals in July, when the MCMC invited eligible telecommunications licensees to submit draft plans under the Universal Service Provision framework.
 The initiative involves building a 5,582km submarine cable network comprising four interconnected segments and 10 landing stations to link Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
 Telekom Malaysia will be responsible for developing and deploying four submarine cable segments, including the associated marine and land works, transmission systems, power feeding equipment and network management systems.
 However, Telekom Malaysia said it is still reviewing the terms and conditions of the approval. The project's implementation and financial impact will depend on formal acceptance of the notification and fulfilment of the stipulated requirements.
 The SALAM network, for which RM2 billion was allocated under the government's Budget 2026, is aimed at improving connectivity and providing greater redundancy to reduce the risk of service disruptions.
 The project is also expected to support the expansion of broadband and 5G services, as well as emerging digital industries such as cloud computing, data centres and artificial intelligence, strengthening Malaysia's digital economy.
 Shares of Telekom Malaysia were down eight sen or about 1% to RM7.75, valuing the state-owned fixed-line operator at RM29.74 billion at Tuesday's noon break.
